chunks: God has verily bought the souls and possessions of the faithful in exchange for a promise of Paradise. They fight in the cause of God, and kill and are killed. This is a promise incumbent on Him, as in the Torah, so the Gospel and the Qur'an. And who is more true to his promise than God? So rejoice at the bargain you have made with Him; for this will be triumph supreme.
ai.seo_question: What is the covenant between God and the believers regarding Paradise and striving in His cause?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often linked to the concept of *al-Bay'* (the divine transaction), emphasizing that believers voluntarily sell their souls to God, mirroring the ultimate sacrifice of Imam al-Husayn (AS) at Karbala. The mention of the Torah and Gospel serves as *tawatur* (widespread attestation) across the three major Abrahamic scriptures, validating the promise of Paradise for those who strive in God's cause. This covenant underscores that true success (*al-fawz al-'azim*) is achieved through faithful adherence to this divine contract, prioritizing spiritual gain over material life.
